title: StarRocks cert-rotate: Vault Agent re-render + rolling FE/BE restart
description: The nexus-cli cert-rotate verb for StarRocks: force a fresh mTLS leaf from the starrocks-server PKI role (Vault Agent re-render + split), then a rolling restart per node to pick up the new cert (StarRocks reads the keystore at start). FE quorum + tablet replicas keep the cluster available during the rolling restart.

observe.what: current leaf serial on a Follower FE -- record as $SERIAL_BEFORE

steps.command: ssh -i $NEXUS_SSH_KEY nexusadmin@192.168.70.32 'sudo rm -f /opt/starrocks/fe/conf/tls/bundle.pem; sudo systemctl restart nexus-vault-agent.service; sleep 6; sudo /usr/local/sbin/starrocks-tls-split.sh /opt/starrocks/fe/conf/tls starrocks; sudo openssl x509 -in /opt/starrocks/fe/conf/tls/server.crt -noout -serial'

observe.what: a NEW serial (!= $SERIAL_BEFORE) -- the rotated leaf is on disk
the rolled Follower rejoins Alive=true with the rotated cert; the other 2 FE kept the quorum available during the restart (rolling, one node at a time)

whatProves: cert-rotate forces a fresh Vault-PKI leaf + re-renders the on-node TLS material; a rolling per-node restart picks it up while the FE quorum + tablet replicas keep the cluster available -- the 90-day rotation path the StarRocksAdapter cert-rotate verb triggers.
